d: the main question that a study tries to answer

d: the results or discoveries of a piece of research
ex: The main findings are presented in the next chapter.

d: to study something in detail to understand it

d: to mention a source in your writing as evidence or support
ex: Always cite the author and the year of publication.

d: a short summary of a research paper placed at its beginning
ex: The abstract must not exceed two hundred and fifty words.

d: a plan that explains what you want to research and how

d: a specific thing that a project tries to achieve

d: money given for a specific research project

d: to read and change a text to make it better
ex: She revised her introduction after reading the comments.

d: to check a text for spelling and grammar mistakes
ex: Please proofread your thesis before you submit it.

d: a note at the bottom of a page giving extra information or a source
ex: The footnote gives the full reference of the case.

d: a list of all the books and articles used in a work

d: a general direction in which something is changing

d: to decide that something is true after thinking about the evidence

d: a statement that something is true, often without proof
ex: The claim is not supported by any evidence.

d: a set of reasons used to show that something is true
ex: The strongest argument is based on three court decisions.

d: one of several things that influence a result
ex: Cost is the main factor in the decision.

d: a strong effect that something has on a person or situation

d: to examine a subject carefully to learn more about it

d: to study something carefully to discover facts
ex: The researchers investigated why some appeals fail.

d: to look at something closely and in detail

d: to study and evaluate existing work or documents

d: to explain exactly what a word or idea means

d: a particular way of dealing with a problem or subject

d: the situation in which something happens, needed to understand it
